To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insulin secretory defect is the primary defect in both type 1 and 2 diabetes and that the secretory defect is caused by β-cell dysfunction in type 1 diabetes and β-cell mass reduction in type 2.

1) the β-cell response to glucose and other nutrients is impaired by a defect in insulin secretion that is independent of insulin resistance; 2) the defect is due to a decrease in the number of functional insulin secretory granules (ISG), which results from a decrease in the β-cell mass; 3) β-cell mass is decreased by an increased apoptosis and/or reduced proliferation of the β-cell mass, and 4) the β-cell defect is reversible, at least in type
the insulin secretory defect in type 2 patients with diabetes results from a loss of β-cell function and that β-cell dysfunction is due to the accumulation of intracellular lipids.

the following: 1) the mechanisms that control insulin secretion and the factors that affect it; 2) β-cell biology, especially the mechanisms that lead to β-cell death; and 3) the factors that affect β-cell mass.
